thread:
incident-bot: 🔔 PagerDuty: service=embed-serve-us-west severity=high — page fired for elevated 5xx rate after recent canary rollout. link: https://pd.example/INC12345

pagerduty-bot: Autopage -> eng-oncall. Escalation policy: oncall->sre->infra-leads.

tara: ack. I'm on it — grabbing logs and metrics. anyone with access to the canary namespace?

miguel: I have cluster access. seeing a spike in kv-cache miss rate and OOMs on a few pods. looks like the new quant path may be hitting edge memory usage.

lucy: that's the staged rollout v1.12.3 we pushed 02:15 UTC. can we pause traffic to canary?

tara: yes — pausing traffic now. running traffic split -> 0% to canary.

deploy-bot: Traffic routing update: service/embed-serve-us-west traffic_split canary -> 0%. (cmd: rtr update --service embed-serve-us-west --canary 0)

pagerduty-bot: ack recorded by tara at 1795001055. next escalation in 9m if unacked.

sanjay: quick impact check — customer-facing: embeddings are failing intermittently for some customers in us-west behind the canary. not global yet. magnitude: ~6% requests 5xx elevated p50->500ms p99->3s.

miguel: digging into pod logs: repeated spikes from quant-kernel allocation around model shard load. stack: 
```
E/quant: alloc failed size=768MB at src/quant/alloc.c:412
warning: kernel fallback -> host memcpy
```

lucy: if quant path is failing we can temporarily switch canary to use fallback model-variant (float16) or just rollback. which is faster?

tara: patching canary to fallback variant might leave bad artifact in registry. given customer impact and uncertain load pattern, recommend rollback to v1.12.2.

jordan: +1 rollback. I'll own postmortem and take notes here. who will execute?

lucy: I can run rollback. steps: 
1) promote v1.12.2 to stable
2) set canary image to v1.12.2 and ramp to 100%
3) monitor errors for 15m
Commands: 
```bash
# promote
registry promote embed-service v1.12.2 --to stable
# update canary
kubectl set image deploy/embed-canary embed=image:1.12.2 -n us-west
# ramp
rtr update --service embed-serve-us-west --canary 100
```

tara: lucy — go for it. miguel keep an eye on memory and OOMs while we flip. i'll coordinate comms.

lucy: running promote now.

deploy-bot: registry: promoted embed-service:v1.12.2 -> stable by lucy at 1795001500.

lucy: updated canary image to v1.12.2 and ramping to 100%.

deploy-bot: traffic_split update: canary -> 100% completed.

miguel: initial metrics after rollback: error rate dropping in canary pods within 30s. p50 back to baseline, p99 trending down. memory stable.

pagerduty-bot: manual note: incident acknowledged and mitigated via rollback at 1795001780.

tara: good. I'm going to suppress noisy alerts for the next 20m while we watch. /alerts silence embed-serve-us-west 20m — please don't unmute unless customer-facing regression or new symptoms.

incident-bot: alert suppression set: 20m for embed-serve-us-west. reason: mitigation-in-progress (rollback).

sanjay: reaching out to the affected customers with a status update. I'll post the draft in #customer-success for review.

jordan: I'll start the incident page and grab timelines. assigning Sev3 for now until we confirm full recovery.

lucy: a note for postmortem — suspect interaction between quant-kernel memory allocation and host kernel on that GPU type (a100-v2 in us-west). need to check kernel selection and memory caps.

miguel: agree — will collect heap dumps and kernel logs and upload to /incidents/INC12345/artifacts.

tara: handing off monitoring to miguel for the 30m watch cycle. i'll jump back if anything flares. thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: summary: PagerDuty fired -> ack by tara -> rollback to v1.12.2 by lucy -> error rate decreasing -> alerts suppressed for 20m -> handoff to miguel for watch. Incident ticket: INC12345.

pagerduty-bot: closing note: no further escalation needed. Escalation policy reset.

miguel: monitoring looks stable at 1795004600. will keep artifacts and notes in the ticket. jordan — ping me if you need logs for the postmortem.

jordan: captured. I'll schedule a 1hr IR sync tomorrow 10:00 UTC and post findings. owners: lucy (rollback/rollback test), miguel (heap/kernel logs), tara (comm + timeline), jordan (postmortem).

incident-bot: thread closed for active mitigation; reopen if errors spike > baseline.
